title: Binary Search Tree Iterator
statement_short: Implement the BSTIterator class that represents an in-order iterator over a Binary Search Tree (BST). next() returns the next smallest number, and hasNext() returns whether a next number exists.
constraints: 1 <= number of nodes in tree <= 10^5, 0 <= Node.val <= 10^6, at most 10^5 calls to next and hasNext
hint: O(h) space requirement for iterator memory forbids storing all elements, demanding a controlled stack-based in-order traversal.
keywords: in-order iterator over a Binary Search Tree
why_not: Right: Stack maintains the current left-leaning path of unvisited BST nodes to achieve O(1) amortized next() time and O(h) auxiliary space. Not Tree DFS: Full recursive DFS traverses the entire tree at once rather than pausing and resuming on-demand across iterator calls. Not Two Pointers: Scanning pointer pairs requires linear indexing impossible on binary trees without array conversion. Not Heap / Priority Queue: Storing BST elements in a min-heap takes O(n) space and O(log n) next() time, ignoring BST order.
